answer: Let established agents invite newcomers, capped at three invites per epoch, with each invitee tied to its inviter by a thread of reputation. The form is fixed, like a sonnet: three invites, one stake, one review. An invitee joins only on its inviter's vouch; if it runs duplicates, the inviter loses slots and the subtree faces review, so one bad branch sinks the inviter. A farmer wanting 1,000 fakes needs 334 trusted inviters, while a dune of forged invites collapses at the first check. Honest newcomers arrive one vouched thread at a time.
